Microscopic vortex braiding from many-body Berry phases
Lu Zhang, Shang-qiang Ning, Hoi Chun Po, Xue-Yang Song, and Xuzhe Ying
∗ †
Department of Physics, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Clear Water Bay, Hong Kong, China and
Center for Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics,
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Clear Water Bay, Hong Kong, China
(Dated: October 30, 2026)
Kitaev’s sixteen-fold way relates (2+1)D invertible fermionic phases to bosonic topological or-
ders obtained by gauging fermion parity, where the statistics of π-vortices are determined by the
Majorana Chern number ν mod16. For even ν , the vortices obey Abelian fusion yet can carry
M M
nontrivial braiding phases that are subtle to access microscopically. We show that these vortex
braiding phases can be extracted as a many-body Berry phase accumulated along a fully gapped
adiabatic cycle that interpolates between the four twisted boundary conditions on a torus. We
demonstrate the computation in free-fermion lattice models with tunable ν . We further provide
M
an interpretation of vortex braiding phase in terms of fermion-parity fractionalization. Utilizing a
bilayer construction and gauging only the total fermion parity, a toric code topological order en-
riched by a global Z symmetry is realized. The symmmetry fractionalization data dictates the
